issues.description: The problem statement/UML requires a class named `Farm`, but the template file `src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java` declares `public class AnimalFarm`. This breaks the mapping between task instructions/tests (which refer to `Farm`) and the starter code students are expected to modify.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template's top-level class from `AnimalFarm` to `Farm` so `Farm.java` contains `public class Farm` as required by the UML/problem statement.

issues.description: The template `src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java` is syntactically invalid: inside `singFarmSong()` it contains a stray `package de.tum.cit.ase;` declaration and an embedded duplicate `public class AnimalFarm { ... }` block. This prevents the template from compiling, blocking students from starting the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the nested `package` declaration and the duplicated embedded `public class AnimalFarm { ... }` block from inside `singFarmSong()`, leaving only a valid method body stub.

issues.description: The problem statement/UML specifies a helper method `singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal)`, but the template declares `private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)` with the parameter commented out. This prevents implementing the required behavior without first changing the method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template signature to `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` (and ensure the `Animal` type exists in the template) to match the UML and allow implementation.
